speakers.speaker: Moderator
speakers.text: Welcome to the panel. Today we are discussing how the groundwater management area responds when monitoring shows the aquifer is still declining.

speakers.speaker: District manager
speakers.text: Our groundwater conservation district adopted new pumping rules last year. Withdrawal permits now depend on drawdown measured at the monitoring wells, and the GCD board reviews them each season.

speakers.speaker: Hydrogeologist
speakers.text: The extensometers tell the real story. Compaction in the clay layers continues even after water levels recover, so land subsidence we see today reflects depletion from twenty years ago. A MODFLOW model with subsidence packages helps us explain that lag to stakeholders.

speakers.speaker: Policy analyst
speakers.text: Governance is the hard part. Regulation has to balance agricultural production, municipal supply for growing cities, and long-term protection of the aquifer. Decision support tools only help if the management rules are transparent.

speakers.speaker: Moderator
speakers.text: Thank you all. The GMA will publish the updated desired future conditions for public comment next month.
